content.title: L3Harris Stock Rises. Guidance Was Confusing.
content.summary: Defense contractor  L3Harris  Technologies presented a mixed picture as it reported fourth-quarter earnings and issued confusing guidance.  Fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.86 a share topped the $2.76 a share analysts had forecast.  Revenue across all of the defense contractor’s business segments fell short of forecasts, with the exception of its integrated mission systems unit, which brought in $1.72 billion in the quarter, topping analysts’ calls for $1.64 billion.

content.title: Meta stock price soars on strong Q4 ad sales. Spending on AI is way up, too
content.summary: Expenses for the Facebook and Instagram parent company grew 40% to $35.15 billion in the fourth quarter, but investors seem not to care.

content.title: Meta posts stronger-than-expected Q4 results though costs continue to soar
content.summary: Meta's fourth-quarter results jumped past Wall Street's expectations thanks to solid advertising revenue, sending shares sharply higher in after-hours trading Wednesday.  “Once again, Meta surpassed analysts’ earnings expectations for the quarter, cementing its position as one of the world’s most dominant media companies," said Debra Aho Williamson, chief analyst at Sonata Insights.  Meta's expenses, which the company already warned will be significantly higher this year, grew 40% to $35.15 billion.

content.title: Amphenol Blows Past Earnings Estimates. The Stock Sinks 12%.
content.summary: Amphenol  posted fourth-quarter earnings and sales that topped consensus views and issued a solid outlook for the current quarter.  Before the opening bell Wednesday,  Amphenol  reported adjusted earnings of 97 cents a share from sales of $6.4 billion, outstripping Wall Street’s forecasts.  Analysts tracked by FactSet expected adjusted earnings of 93 cents a share from sales of $6.2 billion.

content.title: Tesla’s Fourth-Quarter Earnings Are Almost Here. Don’t Expect Them to Be Good.
content.summary: Tesla’s fourth-quarter earnings are due to be released after Wednesday’s market close.  For the quarter, Wall Street analysts tracked by FactSet are looking for earnings per share of 43 cents from sales of $24.6 billion.  A year ago, Tesla reported EPS of 73 cents from sales of $25.7 billion.
